📡 Iran prioritizes peace, respects for rights, calls for lifting of sanctions: Pezeshkian

📌 Tehran, IRNA — President Masoud Pezeshkian has emphasized that Iran prioritizes peace and seeks respect for its international rights and the lifting of sanctions, stressing that Tehran does not seek war or its continuation despite the suffering inflicted on the Iranian people.

Speaking during a meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in India on Saturday, Pezeshkian said that Iran is committed to strengthening ties with neighboring and Muslim countries. He said Iran has no problems with its Muslim neighbors, arguing that the United States seeks to create divisions among friendly nations.
​
Pezeshkian said regional instability has its roots in US and European policies and Israeli crimes, saying independent countries should be allowed to determine their own future.
​
Pezeshkian stressed the need for solidarity among Muslim countries, saying the region does not need a foreign police force. He argued that territorial integrity and regional security can only be achieved by countries in the region.
​
He also referred to the recent conflict, saying Iran was attacked without justification, and its Leader, commanders, scientists, and children were killed. He said the Islamic Republic had no option but to defend itself, including by targeting military bases in neighboring countries used in attacks against Iran.
​
The president referred to internal unrest before the 40-day war, saying enemies armed some elements inside Iran and fomented unrest, with innocent people caught up in tragic events. He said adversaries expected Iran to surrender within days, stressing that the country would never surrender and would continue defending its national rights.
​
For his part, Ibrahim condemned US and Israeli attacks on Iran, saying Malaysia had opposed the aggression from the beginning. He said Iran’s territorial integrity and sovereignty were highly respected by Malaysia and praised Iranian resilience.
​
The prime minister expressed support for stronger Iran–Malaysia relations, saying both sides would explore opportunities in trade, economics, education and other sectors.

💬 AEOI chief heads to Vienna for attending IAEA GC meeting

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) has traveled to Vienna to attend the 70th IAEA General Conference and hold talks with diplomats on nuclear cooperation.

Mohammad Eslami left Tehran for Vienna on Saturday at the head of a delegation of AEOI officials to take part in the annual General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
​
During the trip, Eslami will address the conference and meet ambassadors and representatives from various countries to discuss nuclear cooperation, scientific and technological exchanges, and bilateral and international engagement.
​
AEOI deputies and officials are likewise scheduled to meet foreign representatives to review areas of nuclear cooperation during the event.
​
The 70th Regular Session of the IAEA General Conference will be held from September 14 to 18 at the Vienna International Center, Austria, where high-ranking officials and representatives from IAEA member states will consider a range of issues in the nuclear field, according to an announcement shared on the agency’s official website.

💬 India seeks to expand ties with Iran, foreign ministry spokesperson tells IRNA

📌 Tehran, IRNA – India seeks to further expand its relations with Iran, the spokesperson for the Indian Foreign Ministry has told IRNA, highlighting cooperation and joint projects between the two countries in various fields.

Randhir Jaiswal spoke with IRNA’s correspondent on Saturday on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi.
​
“India-Iran relations are very warm and historic, which are rooted in thousands of years of friendly ties between the two peoples,” Jaiswal said, expressing hope that “these relations will develop further.”
​
Commenting on the US war of aggression against Iran, the Indian diplomat said New Delhi seeks peace and believes issues concerning Iran should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.
​
The interview was conducted as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is in New Delhi to attend the heads-of-state and government summit of BRICS on September 12 and 13.
​
The president arrived in India on Friday and met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

🌍 Iran, Russia stress expansion of bilateral ties

📌 Moscow, IRNA — Deputy Foreign Minister for Administrative and Financial Affairs Mehdi Sobhani and Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation for Asian Affairs Andrey Rudenko have underlined their shared determination to expand bilateral ties.

During the meeting on Friday, the two sides reviewed the latest situation of bilateral ties and major joint projects, including the Rasht–Astara railway, and emphasized the need to further develop these relations.
​
The performance of the embassies of both countries and ways to resolve their problems were also discussed during the meeting.
​
Earlier on Thursday, Sobhani had also met with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister for CIS Affairs Galuzin Mikhail Yuryevich and exchanged views on regional developments and bilateral cooperation.
